messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
A 60-year-old female presented to the emergency room with a sudden onset of severe headache associated with vomiting. On the administration of a CT scan of the brain, subarachnoid hemorrhage was observed, and an aneurysm was suspected. The patient underwent CT cerebral angiogram, and a bilobed anterior communicating artery aneurysm was discovered, projecting anterosuperiorly with a size of 8 x 7 x 5 mm. On the fourth day of ictus, the patient underwent right pterional craniotomy and clipping of the aneurysm. Following surgery, the patient developed right-sided ptosis that advanced to complete right-sided oculomotor nerve paralysis with a dilated and nonreacting pupil. A CT scan of the brain was performed, but no hematoma or infarct was noted. The patient was discharged on the eighth postoperative day and kept under regular follow-up in our outpatient department.

Discharge Condition:
Stable with recovered oculomotor nerve paralysis.

Course of Treatment:
The patient was administered antiedema measures, anticonvulsant, analgesic, and Nimodipine. The medication was continued for a total of 21 days following the ictus.

Discharge Instructions:
The patient is advised to follow up with their healthcare provider regularly.

Follow-up Care:
The patient underwent a Magnetic Resonance Imaging scan of the brain with venogram to rule out any infarct or thrombosis of the cavernous sinus after a week of discharge. No abnormalities were noted. The patient came for follow-up on the 61st postoperative day, and her ptosis had fully recovered. A full recovery of the ocular motor nerve paralysis was noted. The patient was advised to continue regular follow-up with their healthcare provider.

Discharge Medications:
Medications are not listed as per case report instructions.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The principal diagnosis is a subarachnoid hemorrhage from a ruptured anterior communicating artery aneurysm. ICD-10-AM codes this as I60 (nontraumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage), with the specific code I60.2 for an anterior communicating artery source.

The postoperative oculomotor nerve palsy is a complication, so it would be coded as an additional diagnosis rather than the principal one.

**I60**
